name: FontPair
tagline: A curated browser of Google Fonts pairings with live previews and copyable CSS.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software here is thin: load the Google Fonts catalog, render two fonts together, let someone change the sample text, emit the CSS. An agent can do all of that in a sitting, including a seeded list of a few hundred plausible pairings, because font pairing advice is everywhere in training data and the fonts themselves are free. What you cannot one-shot is somebody's eye, and the site's real product is a human deciding which pairs are actually worth showing. That is a taste gap, not a technical one, and for a personal tool it is survivable: you only need pairings you like, not pairings that hold up for a million strangers. Build it, keep the ten combinations you keep reaching for, delete the rest.
coreLoopDIY: A local static page that browses the Google Fonts catalog, previews any two fonts as heading and body with editable sample text, and copies the import plus CSS.
requirements: a Google Fonts Developer API key in .env, or a checked-in catalog snapshot
whatYouLose: Curation by someone with actual typographic taste, which is the entire point of the original
New pairings added over time as the catalog grows
Any sense of whether a pair is overused, dated, or quietly broken at small sizes
Polished category browsing, thumbnails, and pairing pages that look good enough to send to a client
Non-Google foundries, which a free-fonts-only build will never touch
moatNotes: The moat is a curated list and a reputation for taste, both of which are content, not code. Content moats leak: an LLM has read every font pairing blog post ever written.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because deciding is the work. Anyone can render two typefaces side by side; the value is arriving at a page where someone already threw out the 900 combinations that look wrong and left you with the ones that do not. If you are picking type for client work under deadline, paying for a shortlist from someone whose eye you trust is cheaper than an afternoon of scrolling your own homemade grid.
notes: One of the rare cases where the DIY version is technically identical and aesthetically worse, and that may be fine for you.
prompt:
Build a local, offline-friendly font pairing browser. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Vite + vanilla TypeScript + plain CSS. No React, no UI framework, no Tailwind.
- One Node build script, no database, no server at runtime.

Step 1, catalog:
- Write scripts/fetch-catalog.ts that calls the Google Fonts Developer API using GOOGLE_FONTS_API_KEY from .env and writes src/data/fonts.json with family, category, variants, subsets.
- Commit a small fallback fonts.json (about 200 popular families) so the app runs with no key at all. Document both paths in README.
- Include .env.example with GOOGLE_FONTS_API_KEY=

Step 2, seed pairings:
- Create src/data/pairings.json with 60 or more curated pairs, each: { id, headingFamily, bodyFamily, note } where note is one short sentence on why it works. Use well-known, safe combinations from the Google catalog. Do not invent families that are not in fonts.json; validate at build time and fail loudly if a family is missing.

Step 3, the app:
- Grid of pairing cards. Each card renders a real specimen: heading line, subhead, two paragraphs of body copy.
- Load fonts by injecting Google Fonts stylesheet links on demand, only for visible cards, using IntersectionObserver.
- Detail view for a pair: editable sample text (contenteditable or textarea), sliders for heading size, body size, line height, letter spacing, and a light/dark toggle.
- Custom pair builder: two searchable comboboxes over the full catalog, filter by category (serif, sans-serif, display, handwriting, monospace).
- Copy button that outputs the @import line plus a CSS block with the current sizes and spacing. Also a second button for an HTML link tag version.
- Favorites saved to localStorage, with a Favorites filter. Export favorites to JSON, import it back.
- Keyboard: / focuses search, r shuffles a random pair, f toggles favorite.

Out of scope, do not build:
- Uploading or self-hosting custom font files, non-Google foundries, licensing checks, sharing links, screenshots, or any server.

Deliver: working npm run dev and npm run build, a README explaining the API key is optional, and no secrets in source.
